topic: The Visual Heart of Linear Algebra: Grids, Transforms, and Determinants
target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students beginning their journey in Linear Algebra.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Vector as a Navigation Instruction
lecture_lines: Imagine a vector as a navigation instruction.
We start on a standard 2D coordinate grid.
Every journey begins at the origin point.
This instruction moves three right and two up.
A single arrow represents this specific movement.
animations: Background is #000000. Display a 2D coordinate grid (#555555). Highlight lecture line 1 by changing its color to #00CCFF. Fade in the title "The Vector as Navigation" (#FFFFFF).
Highlight lecture line 2 (#00CCFF). Show a vector [3, 2] represented as a set of numeric coordinates near the origin.
Highlight lecture line 3 (#00CCFF). Pulse a yellow dot (#FFFF00) at (0,0) labeled "Origin".
Highlight lecture line 4 (#00CCFF). Draw a blue dashed line (#00CCFF) from (0,0) to (3,0), then a green dashed line (#33FF33) up to (3,2).
Highlight lecture line 5 (#00CCFF). Draw a thick magenta arrow (#FF3399) from (0,0) to (3,2). Label it "[3, 2]".

sections.title: The DNA of Space: Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: Every vector is built from two fundamental pieces.
Basis vector "i" points one unit right.
Basis vector "j" points one unit up.
All vectors are combinations of these two units.
Together, they form the DNA of our space.
animations: Highlight lecture line 1 (#00FFCC). Display a standard grid (#555555).
Highlight lecture line 2 (#00FFCC). Draw a red arrow (#FF0000) from (0,0) to (1,0) and label it "i-hat".
Highlight lecture line 3 (#00FFCC). Draw a green arrow (#00FF00) from (0,0) to (0,1) and label it "j-hat".
Highlight lecture line 4 (#00FFCC). Show the vector [3, -2] being composed by 3 red i-hat arrows and 2 inverted green j-hat arrows.
Highlight lecture line 5 (#00FFCC). The entire grid pulses in white (#FFFFFF) to emphasize that i and j are the basis.

sections.title: Matrices as Morphing Machines
lecture_lines: Matrices act as machines that transform the entire grid.
We only need to track where i and j land.
Linear transformations keep grid lines parallel and evenly spaced.
Watch this matrix rotate the plane ninety degrees counter-clockwise.
The landing spots of i and j define the transformation.
animations: Highlight lecture line 1 (#FFD700). Show i-hat (#FF0000) and j-hat (#00FF00) on a grid.
Highlight lecture line 2 (#FFD700). Transform the grid: i-hat moves to (0,1) and j-hat moves to (-1,0).
Highlight lecture line 3 (#FFD700). Draw parallel grid lines that remain straight and evenly spaced during the transformation.
Highlight lecture line 4 (#FFD700). Animate labels for i-hat and j-hat following their new positions at (0,1) and (-1,0).
Highlight lecture line 5 (#FFD700). Rotate a "90 deg" symbol (#FFFFFF) around the origin.

sections.title: The Determinant: Measuring the 'Stretch'
lecture_lines: The determinant measures how much transformations scale areas.
Watch this unit square stretch after a transformation.
An area tripled means the determinant is three.
animations: Highlight lecture line 1 (#FF6600). Fade in a standard coordinate grid (#555555).
Highlight lecture line 2 (#FF6600). Create a 1x1 yellow square (#FFFF00) with corners (0,0) and (1,1).
Highlight lecture line 3 (#FF6600). Transform the grid so the square scales by factor 3.
Highlight lecture line 4 (#FF6600). Display text "Area = 3" and "det(A) = 3" (#00FF00) near the shape.
Highlight lecture line 5 (#FF6600). Change transformation so the grid collapses into a single white line (#FFFFFF); display "det(A) = 0" (#FF0000).

sections.title: Synthesis: Solving Systems Geometrically
lecture_lines: We can solve systems of equations through geometric visualization.
We look for a vector that transforms to destination b.
Vector x is the original instruction leading to b.
animations: Highlight lecture line 1 (#CC00FF). Show the equation "Ax = b" (#FFFFFF) at the top.
Highlight lecture line 2 (#CC00FF). Show a target vector "b" (#FF3399) on a transformed grid.
Highlight lecture line 3 (#CC00FF). Show a vector "x" (#00CCFF) on the original grid being transformed until it lands exactly on "b".
